blocks.orig: Say hello to one of our bestsellers! If you want to see the three most beautiful parks in northern Tanzania, our 8-day safari is the perfect option. You will start your safari in the kingdom of the elephants, Tarangire National Park. Visit the famous Serengeti, home to an abundance of wildlife as well as the impressive wildebeest migration. And the striking Ngorongoro Crater, a natural wonder with the world’s highest concentration of wildlife. These are two of Africa’s Seven Natural Wonders you can witness on this amazing safari.
blocks.html: Meet one of our bestsellers! Our 8-day safari is the ideal choice if you would like to visit the three most beautiful parks of northern Tanzania. Your safari begins in Tarangire National Park, the kingdom of the elephants. You go on to the famous Serengeti, where you find abundant wildlife and the impressive wildebeest migration, and to the striking Ngorongoro Crater, a natural wonder with the highest density of wildlife in the world. On this amazing safari you get to see two of Africa’s Seven Natural Wonders.

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: A question we hear from many travellers is when to go to Tanzania. The honest reply … no single answer fits everyone. It comes down to what you hope to see, the places you want to visit, your budget and your interests. You can read our detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: On a safari with us in Tanzania you get the chance to discover the country’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our focus, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is for you alone. You decide when each safari day begins and finishes, and on the day itself our experienced guides are happy to help you choose. Perhaps you would like to see the animals at their liveliest around sunrise and sunset, when it is pleasantly cool, or perhaps you would rather finish the afternoon at the pool; the choice is completely yours. Because the wildlife of Tanzania is active at different moments of the day, you’ll get many chances to watch the animals in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, definitely: Tanzania is known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. You can watch these impressive animals (lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo) in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is a safe and friendly country to travel in. You’ll find a welcoming atmosphere, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, so you can enjoy the scenery and wildlife with peace of mind. People are kind, and simple precautions like keeping an eye on your belongings remain sensible, as they would be anywhere in the world. With its natural beauty and warm-hearted people, Tanzania is a wonderful country to visit.

blocks.html: When you step out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your own Your Tanzania Trip guide welcomes you with a broad smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is well known for its big groups of elephants and the huge amount of giant baobab trees. These trees can live for hundreds of years and are actually a source of water for elephants in the dry season as they have a special technique to draw water from them. Besides, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why in this season in Tarangire you can see groups of up to 250 elephants next to many more animals!
blocks.html: Tarangire National Park is famous for its large herds of elephants and its huge number of giant baobab trees. These trees can grow hundreds of years old, and in the dry season they even provide water for the elephants, which use a special technique to get water out of them. On top of that, the Tarangire River is the only water source during the dry season, so at that time of year you can see herds of up to 250 elephants in Tarangire, along with many other animals!

blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park is widely known as the place to go on safari, mainly because of the Great Migration that passes through here. The enormous, stampeding herds are impressive, as are the vast number of predators that live here: over four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas, and hundreds of wild dogs! And of course, plenty of other beautiful animals, which your guide will be delighted to search for together with you. Are you ready for this?
blocks.html: Serengeti National Park is known far and wide as the place for a safari, largely thanks to the Great Migration that moves through it. The huge, thundering herds are impressive, and so is the number of predators living here: more than four thousand lions, more than 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas and hundreds of wild dogs! Plus, of course, many other beautiful animals that your guide will be happy to look for with you. Are you ready?

blocks.orig: The famous Ngorongoro Crater is one of Africa's seven natural wonders. The crater was formed two million years ago when a vast volcano erupted. The fertile lava has created a unique ecosystem, now home to the highest concentration of animals found anywhere in Africa! Once in the crater, thousands of animals such as lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos surround you, and the views are astounding – you won’t know where to look!
blocks.html: The well-known Ngorongoro Crater counts as one of Africa's seven natural wonders. It came into being two million years ago, when a huge volcano erupted. The fertile lava gave rise to a unique ecosystem that now has the highest density of animals anywhere in Africa! Inside the crater you are surrounded by thousands of animals, including lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos, and the views are amazing – you won’t know which way to look!

Having second thoughts? It's also possible to add a few days to your holiday by going to one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day! Depending on when your flight leaves, you can stay at the lodge a little longer before you travel to Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) for your flight home.
